clue.text: Doc times new delivery, at home

indicators.note: a new delivery of these words hands them over in a fresh order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A doctor repeatedly attends a fresh birth in a patient's own house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new delivery' reads as a home birth, but it tells you to rearrange the letters of DOC and TIMES.
explanation.definitionFit: Domestic matters belong to the household, the sphere of life lived in one's own house.

clue.text: Risqué or risky

definitions.meaning: risqué means bold or slightly indecent
risky means hazardous, as a bold venture is

explanation.surface: Is something a little racy or simply dangerous?
explanation.definitionFit: A daring joke is near the knuckle and a daring stunt is hazardous: both senses fit the bold adjective.

clue.text: From Scottish isle note surfacing fish

parts.note: Mull is an island of the Inner Hebrides

indicators.note: in a down clue, surfacing means coming upward, so the word for the note is read from bottom to top

parts.note: te is a note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A fish rises to the surface off a Hebridean island.
explanation.definitionFit: The mullet is a common food fish, grey or red.

clue.text: He offers wine to banker waving lire

parts.note: a crossword banker is something with banks, a river; the Somme is a river in France

indicators.note: waving the letters about shakes them into a new order

explanation.surface: A bank employee waves Italian banknotes while offering a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'banker' suggests a financier, but in crosswords it is a river, here the SOMME. 'waving' rearranges LIRE into LIER.
explanation.definitionFit: A sommelier is the restaurant's wine waiter, who recommends and serves wine to diners.

clue.text: Stop marine pollution or he takes off

indicators.note: pollution corrupts and fouls, so the letters of the preceding words are mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: An environmental slogan: halt sea contamination or the culprit leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: To take someone off is to mimic them, which is what an impressionist does.

clue.text: Wine taken from secure pouch

parts.note: to bar a door is to secure it
a sac is a pouch, as in anatomy

explanation.surface: A bottle of wine is pulled out of a locked bag.
explanation.definitionFit: Barsac is a sweet white Bordeaux from the commune of that name near Sauternes.

clue.text: Slogan of the commercial era

parts.note: an ad is a commercial, an advertisement
an age is an era

explanation.surface: A catchphrase defines the age of television advertising.
explanation.definitionFit: A saw or proverb, like a slogan, is a short pithy saying repeated often.

clue.text: Dab hands at water-skiing, it transpires

parts.note: water-skiing is a watersport, here loosely surfing
aces are experts, dab hands at something

explanation.surface: Experts on water skis turn out to be impressive, it seems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it transpires' sounds like an aside, but 'transpires' is the definition, with 'at' and 'it' joining.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that comes to light or emerges, as a fact does, can be said to come up or be revealed.

clue.text: Scotsman turning up, off-piste, seeking temporary place for shelter

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: Mac is a stock name for a Scot

indicators.note: off here means out of order, so the letters of the word for a ski run are jumbled

explanation.surface: A Scottish skier, having strayed from the marked run, looks for somewhere to bed down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off-piste' looks like skiing jargon; 'off' rearranges PISTE into PSITE.
explanation.definitionFit: A tent pitch, where campers stay a few nights under canvas, is a temporary shelter.

clue.text: Chunk of bread soaks up liquid from pickled fish

parts.note: a roll is a small piece of bread
mops means wipes up a spill

explanation.surface: A piece of bread mops up the juice from some marinated herring.
explanation.definitionFit: A rollmop is a fillet of herring rolled up and marinated in vinegar.

clue.text: In either direction, you'll see grass

indicators.note: reading the word forwards or backwards gives the same letters, a palindrome

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: Whichever way you look, there is grass.
explanation.definitionFit: Marram is a coarse dune grass planted to bind sand.

clue.text: I hurt man in a brawl -but who cares?

indicators.note: a brawl is a free-for-all scuffle, so the words are thrown into disorder

parts.note: the fodder as printed holds only two As; the setter's letters need a third A to make the twelve

explanation.surface: A brawler shrugs off injuring someone, asking who cares.
explanation.walkthrough: The fodder as printed is one A short; the setter needed another A to rearrange into the answer. 'brawl' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A humanitarian is a philanthropist, someone concerned for the welfare of people.

clue.text: Rifle butt is grasped by respectable relative

indicators.note: being grasped means being held inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: nice in an older sense means proper or respectable

indicators.note: the butt of a rifle is its end, so take the last letter

explanation.surface: A decent family member holds a gun by its stock.
explanation.definitionFit: A niece is a sibling's daughter, a family relation.

clue.text: With their aid, travelling west from spa, joined up with our members

annotationWithheld.why: With their aid, travelling west from spa, joined up with our members (5,4): SPA and MET reversed give APS and TEM, but no reading of 'our members' gives ROU before them; likely an OCR or setter slip
annotationWithheld.clue: With their aid, travelling west from spa, joined up with our members

clue.text: Recovery likely from it with fresh application of liniment — or a grim end?

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter
applying the words afresh puts their letters in a new order

explanation.surface: A rub with liniment should cure it, unless the outcome is fatal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'end' takes the last letter of 'grim', M, which joins LINIMENT, OR and A in the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: A small complaint such as a cold is something a patient usually gets over.

clue.text: Views and places spoilt

definitions.note: plural, while the answer is a singular noun; a scenic outlook is a collection of views

indicators.note: spoilt means damaged, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Beauty spots ruined by development.
explanation.definitionFit: A rural scene is a view of countryside, a picture of open scenery.

clue.text: Weep over returning soldier — it's the physical bond

indicators.note: in a down clue one word over another covers it, so it sits outside

parts.note: to lament is to weep or mourn

indicators.note: returning means the word is turned back to front

parts.note: GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: Someone cries over a soldier coming home, an emotional tie.
explanation.definitionFit: A ligament is the tough band of tissue binding bones together at a joint.

clue.text: Sinks the ship despite drains aboard

definitions.meaning: to scupper a vessel is to scuttle it deliberately
holes in a ship's side letting water off the deck

explanation.surface: The vessel goes down even though its deck outlets work.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to wreck or scuttle a vessel; as a noun the openings at deck level carrying water overboard.

clue.text: Trendy bloomers favoured by gods assuming bodily form?

definitions.note: a phrase standing for nouns: embodiments, instances of taking flesh

parts.note: in means fashionable
the carnation's genus Dianthus means flower of Zeus in Greek

explanation.surface: Fashionable flowers loved by deities take on physical shape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomers' are flowers, not knickers; DIANTHUS is Greek for divine flower, hence the gods.
explanation.definitionFit: An incarnation is an embodiment, a spirit or deity taking on flesh.

clue.text: Loop-line in the West

parts.note: a rope with a running noose, as used by cowboys of the American West

explanation.walkthrough: 'Loop-line' suggests a railway branch, but it is a rope ending in a loop.
explanation.definitionFit: A cowboy's lasso is a long rope with a noose, used in ranching country.

clue.text: For a start, has nothing to write to the Queen

parts.note: O is zero, nothing
pen means to write
ER is the royal cipher, Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: To begin, one has nothing to send in a letter to the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done for a start is a beginning, the first item in a sequence.

clue.text: Horse papa also trained to circle the ring

indicators.note: circling something means surrounding it, so one piece is put inside the other
trained means schooled or reshaped, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: Dad's horse, also schooled, is taken round the arena.
explanation.definitionFit: An appaloosa is a spotted North American horse breed.

clue.text: Wild leaps causing a slip

indicators.note: wild means out of control, so the letters are shuffled

explanation.surface: Reckless jumping leads to a fall.
explanation.definitionFit: A lapse is a small error or slip in conduct or concentration.

clue.text: Southwest current joins flood

parts.note: SW is the compass abbreviation
an amp is a unit of electric current

explanation.surface: A south-westerly stream adds to rising floodwater.
explanation.definitionFit: To swamp is to inundate, overwhelm with water.

clue.text: Release politician trapped between river and junction

indicators.note: trapped between two pieces means held inside them

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon
T is a T-junction
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A politician caught between a river and a road junction is freed.
explanation.definitionFit: To excuse someone from a duty is to free them from it.

clue.text: Commendation for First Officer in Titanic disaster

indicators.note: in means put inside the other piece
a disaster wrecks things, so the letters are rearranged
first means only the opening letter of the next word is used

explanation.surface: A ship's officer is praised for conduct in the 1912 sinking.
explanation.definitionFit: A citation is an official mention praising bravery, as in a military award.

clue.text: Maybe put on a cap — it's a hanging matter

annotationWithheld.why: Maybe put on a cap — it's a hanging matter (6): the clue fits TASSEL, a cap's hanging ornament, not the grid's TASSET; no parse gives TASSET
annotationWithheld.clue: Maybe put on a cap — it's a hanging matter

clue.text: Model T version, he speculates

indicators.note: to model something is to reshape it, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man gambles on a new version of the Model T Ford.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Model T' reads as the Ford car; 'Model' is the anagram signal on T and VERSION.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who puts money into ventures hoping for profit is a speculator.
